hook.text: Skin that senses temperature, pressure, and humidity — e-skin wraps sensors in flexible, stretchable biocompatible materials.

buildup.text: Thin-film transistors on polymer substrates create arrays of pressure sensors — matching the sensitivity of human fingertips.

discovery.text: Self-healing e-skin repairs cuts using dynamic polymer bonds — the material reconnects like biological tissue after damage.

twist.text: Powering e-skin is hard — flexible form limits battery options, but triboelectric generators harvest motion energy.

climax.text: E-skin on prosthetic hands gives amputees a sense of touch — pressure signals route through nerve interfaces to the brain.

punchline.text: Feel with electronics — e-skin restores sensation where biology cannot.

quiz.question: How does self-healing electronic skin repair itself?
options: Embedded batteries melt and reseal the damaged area
Dynamic polymer bonds reform after cuts, reconnecting the material like biological tissue healing
A layer of liquid adhesive flows over the damaged region
